summary: This document defines a Management Information Base (MIB) subset for power and energy monitoring of devices, so network management tools can read how much power equipment uses.

eli5.summary: This is a list of meters that lets tools read how much electricity a device is using.

questions: what is the energy object mib
how to monitor power consumption with snmp
what are power states in snmp
subtitle: SNMP MIB modules that let management systems read how much power and energy networked devices use, and what power state they are in.

tldr.problem: Operators want to monitor power state and energy use of routers, switches, power-over-Ethernet endpoints, meters and other devices, in a standard way that management tools can read.
tldr.mechanism: Two SNMP MIB modules, ENERGY-OBJECT-MIB and POWER-ATTRIBUTES-MIB, define tables for power readings, power states, energy over configurable intervals and optional AC power quality, indexed by the ENTITY-MIB physical index.
tldr.outcome: Devices can report power in a scaled, accuracy-labelled way, and management systems can discover and track power states and energy. Write access to some objects makes SNMPv3 security important.

today: RFC 7460 is a Proposed Standard from March 2015, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It works together with the Energy Object Context MIB in RFC 7461.

sections.title: Purpose and Scope
sections.content:
RFC 7460 defines a subset of the Management Information Base (MIB) for energy management of devices in or connected to communication networks. The modules model Power State and energy consumption of networked elements, following the Energy Management Framework (RFC 7326), which in turn is based on the Requirements for Energy Management (RFC 6988).

Target devices include routers, switches, Power over Ethernet endpoints, protocol gateways for building management systems, intelligent meters, home energy gateways, hosts and servers, and sensor proxies. Monitoring extends to a device's components (for example line cards or hard drives) and to attached dependent devices, such as the endpoints behind a PoE switch or a power distribution unit. The scope is broader than RFC 6988, and also covers facility meters, building control gateways and devices that interface with the utility or smart grid.

As with other MIBs, objects are read through SNMP and defined with SMIv2 (RFC 2578, RFC 2579, RFC 2580).
sections.eli5: It is a standard way for all kinds of gadgets, from big network switches to home meters, to tell a computer how much electricity they use.

sections.title: Two MIB Modules and Their Tables
sections.content:
The Energy Monitoring MIB has two independent modules. ENERGY-OBJECT-MIB measures power and energy. POWER-ATTRIBUTES-MIB covers power quality for Energy Objects. Devices and their parts are modelled with the containment tree of the ENTITY-MIB (RFC 6933), and entPhysicalIndex is the main index.

ENERGY-OBJECT-MIB has five tables. eoMeterCapabilitiesTable says which instrumentation each object has. eoPowerTable reports power with units, sign and accuracy. eoPowerStateTable gives information and statistics for each supported Power State. eoEnergyParametersTable configures energy and demand collection, and eoEnergyTable holds the resulting log.

POWER-ATTRIBUTES-MIB has three tables, aligned with IEC 61850 7-2 for alternating current measurements. eoACPwrAttributesTable covers the configuration (single phase, DEL 3 phases or WYE 3 phases), frequency, accuracy, total active, reactive and apparent power, current and voltage. For three-phase power, eoACPwrAttributesDelPhaseTable gives phase-to-phase values for DEL, and eoACPwrAttributesWyePhaseTable gives phase-to-neutral values for WYE. This module is optional.
sections.eli5: Think of two notebooks. One records how much power a gadget uses and how much energy over time. The other, which is optional, records fussy details about the electricity itself.

sections.title: Energy Objects and Power States
sections.content:
Anything that can be monitored is an Energy Object. Its identity and its relationships to other objects (such as metered by, powered by or aggregated by) come from the ENERGY-OBJECT-CONTEXT-MIB in RFC 7461.

An Energy Object may have energy-conservation modes called Power States, with several intermediate energy-saving modes between ON and OFF. eoPowerAdminState is the state requested, eoPowerOperState is the actual state, and a difference between them means the object is still transitioning. eoPowerStateEnterReason records the reason for a change.

Power States belong to a Power State Set, and an object can support several sets at once. Three are currently defined: IEEE1621, DMTF and EMAN (the last from RFC 7326). eoPowerStateTable lists the maximum power in watts for each state, how many times the object entered it (eoPowerStateEnterCount) and the total time spent in it (eoPowerStateTotalTime). An eoPowerStateChange SNMP notification is generated when the state index, operational state or administrative state changes.
sections.eli5: A gadget can be fully on, asleep, or off, and some modes are in between. The tables say which mode it is in, which mode it was asked to be in, and how long it spent in each.

sections.title: Reporting Power Usage
sections.content:
Current power use is reported in eoPower. Its magnitude depends on eoPowerUnitMultiplier: the value in SI units is the base value times 10 raised to the multiplier. So a reading of 3 could mean 3 W, 3 mW, 3 kW or 3 MW. The same mechanism is used for state power, energy and AC power attributes.

Extra objects describe how trustworthy the number is. eoPowerAccuracy is a percentage in hundredths of a percent, from 0 to 10000, where 1010 means accurate to plus or minus 10.1 percent, and 0 means unknown or not applicable. eoPowerMeasurementCaliber says how the value was obtained (unavailable, unknown, actual, estimated or static), and eoPowerMeasurementLocal says whether it was measured at the device or from a remote source. A device that cannot measure power reports caliber unavailable and an eoPower of 0.

Accuracy is expressed as an accuracy class rather than the decimal precision used in the ENTITY-SENSOR MIB, because the ANSI and IEC power measurement standards use accuracy classes.
sections.eli5: Along with the number, the device says what unit it is in and how sure it is. Saying 3 means little unless you know whether it is 3 watts or 3 kilowatts.

sections.title: Energy and Demand Measurement
sections.content:
Energy and demand only make sense when power comes from real measurement hardware. If the caliber is unavailable, unknown, estimated or presumed, the energy values are not useful. Collection is configured in eoEnergyParametersTable: the interval length, the number of intervals to keep, the interval mode, and a sample rate used to compute averages. eoEnergyParametersStatus starts and stops logging, and the storage type says whether the row survives a device reload.

There are three interval modes, based on IEC 61850-7-4. Period means non-overlapping intervals, so each start time is the previous start plus the length. Sliding means overlapping intervals. Total means a continuous measurement since the last reset, with the interval number set to one and the length ignored. Several modes can be configured for one object, depending on its capability.

The RFC gives an example: an interval length of 900 seconds (15 minutes), 10 intervals, and a sample rate of 1000 milliseconds. eoEnergyTable then holds consumed, provided and stored energy, an accuracy and the maximum observed energy. For example, eoEnergyConsumed of 100 with a multiplier of 0 is 100 watt-hours. eoEnergyDiscontinuityTime records the sysUpTime of the last interruption of total energy measurement. A management system that polls the table can compute the maximum over a longer period such as a month.
sections.eli5: It is like reading an electricity meter every 15 minutes and writing down the last ten readings, plus the highest one. You can choose to count in separate blocks, in overlapping blocks, or in one long stretch.

sections.title: Discovery and Structure
sections.content:
Most Energy Objects will need ENERGY-OBJECT-CONTEXT-MIB (RFC 7461) as a prerequisite. Every Energy Object MUST implement entPhysicalIndex, entPhysicalClass, entPhysicalName and entPhysicalUUID from the ENTITY-MIB. A network management system first polls the context MIB to discover the objects and their relationships, then reads eoPowerStateTable to find the Power States and maximum power per state, and finally reads POWER-ATTRIBUTES-MIB for power quality.

The MIB is described as a sparse extension of ENERGY-OBJECT-CONTEXT-MIB, and that module SHOULD be implemented. The eoMeterCapabilitiesTable lets an application learn which groups are supported without trial-and-error table walks. The energy table, the AC power attributes and battery information are all optional.
sections.eli5: First the computer asks the gadget what it is and what parts it has. Then it asks what power modes it has, and last it looks at the electrical details if they are provided.

sections.title: Relationship to Other MIBs
sections.content:
The RFC explains how it fits with existing MIBs. Unlike the ENTITY-SENSOR MIB (RFC 3433), it uses accuracy classes and a power-of-ten unit multiplier suited to power measurement. It can map to the ENTITY-STATE MIB (RFC 4268): for example, the standby states unknown, hotStandby and coldStandby could map to the Power States unknown, ready and standby.

For Power over Ethernet (RFC 3621), the Energy Object carries the PoE port and group indexes, or zero when the PoE MIB is not implemented. A UPS MIB (RFC 1628) can run on the same agent without conflict; the UPS itself is then an Energy Object. For LLDP-MED, the endpoint power priority can be identified through the PoE indexes, and the LLDP-MED power source can be mapped onto eoPowerMeasurementLocal. Where the ENTITY-MIB is not implemented, such as in a building gateway, the physical entity value is zero.
sections.eli5: There were already some older lists that talk about sensors, power over network cables and battery backups. This one is built to sit alongside them and to be easy to match up with them.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Some objects are read-write or read-create. Unauthorized changes to eoPowerAdminState (which drives eoPowerOperState) MAY disrupt the power settings and functioning of Energy Objects, and unauthorized changes to eoEnergyParametersTable MAY disrupt energy measurement. SNMP versions before SNMPv3 did not include adequate security, so implementations SHOULD provide the SNMPv3 security features, and deploying earlier versions is NOT RECOMMENDED. Operators must configure access so only legitimate principals can read or change the objects.

The RFC also raises privacy: energy and power monitoring can reveal sensitive information about individuals' activities and habits. Monitoring of individuals and homes should only occur with proper authorization. For IANA, the modules received the identifiers mib-2 228 (IANAPowerStateSet-MIB), 229 (energyObjectMIB) and 230 (powerAttributesMIB), and IANA maintains the PowerStateSet textual convention.
sections.eli5: If a stranger could flip the switches, they could put gadgets to sleep or spoil the readings. Also, a record of power use can show when someone is home. So access must be locked down.
